parole.significato: Any of various types of steamed bread or bun used in Chinese cuisine
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 包 (bāo) or Cantonese 包 (baau1). Cognate of Vietnamese bánh bao.
Borrowed from Mandarin 炒飯 /炒饭 (chǎofàn), possibly originally from Cantonese 炒飯 /炒饭 (caau² faan⁶). Compare Spanish chaufa, chofán

parole.significato: Used at the end of an affirmative declarative sentence to change it into a yes–no question.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 嗎／吗 (ma) or Cantonese 嗎／吗 (maa⁵).

parole.significato: Mother-in-law, (especially) the mother of one's husband.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 婆婆 (pópo, “husband's mother”), Cantonese 婆婆 (po⁴ po⁴⁻², “maternal grandmother”).
From Mandarin 煙 /烟 (yān), 菸 /烟 (yān), or Cantonese 煙 /烟 (jin¹), 菸 /烟 (jin¹, “smoke, specifically opium”). Compare the earlier yen (“strong desire”) and later yen-yen.
